es: Sustituir expresiones crudas por eufemismos y atenuaciones (between jobs, passed away, let go, not the best) al hablar de temas delicados.

teaching.en: Saying «unemployed» can feel blunt, so many people prefer the euphemism «between jobs», which suggests that the situation is only temporary.
teaching.es: Decir «unemployed» puede resultar brusco, así que muchos prefieren el eufemismo «between jobs», que sugiere que la situación es solo temporal.
teaching.explanationEs: Between jobs es un eufemismo: suaviza la situación y deja abierta una salida.

«between jobs», which suggests that the situation is only temporary.

teaching.en: When my elderly neighbour passed away last month, the family asked us not to say «died», because «passed away» sounds softer and more respectful.
teaching.es: Cuando mi vecino mayor falleció el mes pasado, la familia nos pidió que no dijéramos «died», porque «passed away» suena más suave y respetuoso.
teaching.explanationEs: Passed away es más suave que died; elderly es más amable que old.
segments: When my elderly neighbour passed away last month, the family asked us
not to say «died», because «passed away» sounds softer and more respectful.
teaching.audioText: When my elderly neighbour passed away last month, the family asked us not to say «died», because «passed away» sounds softer and more respectful.

teaching.en: The company decided to let go of three workers, so the manager spoke gently and explained that the decision was not about their performance.
teaching.es: La empresa decidió prescindir de tres trabajadores, así que la directora habló con delicadeza y explicó que la decisión no dependía de su rendimiento.
teaching.explanationEs: Let go = forma suave de fire; gently describe el tono con que se da la noticia.
segments: The company decided to let go of three workers, so the manager
spoke gently and explained that the decision was not about their performance.
teaching.audioText: The company decided to let go of three workers, so the manager spoke gently and explained that the decision was not about their performance.

teaching.en: Calling a terrible film «not the best» is a classic understatement: the listener understands perfectly that you did not enjoy it at all.
teaching.es: Llamar «not the best» a una película terrible es una atenuación clásica: el oyente entiende perfectamente que no la disfrutaste en absoluto.
teaching.explanationEs: Not the best rebaja la opinión: dice menos de lo que siente, y el oyente entiende «malo».
segments: Calling a terrible film «not the best» is a classic understatement: the
listener understands perfectly that you did not enjoy it at all.

teaching.en: Estate agents often rely on euphemism: «cosy» can mean tiny, and «full of character» can mean that the building needs a lot of repair.
teaching.es: Los agentes inmobiliarios recurren a menudo al eufemismo: «cosy» puede significar diminuto, y «full of character» que el edificio necesita muchas reparaciones.
teaching.explanationEs: Los anuncios inmobiliarios usan eufemismos; el mensaje real es otro.

teaching.en: There is a time to sugarcoat bad news and a time to be direct, so never beat around the bush when someone needs a clear answer.
teaching.es: Hay momentos para endulzar una mala noticia y momentos para ser directo, así que no te andes por las ramas cuando alguien necesita una respuesta clara.
teaching.explanationEs: Sugarcoat = endulzar; beat around the bush = dar rodeos. Elige según la persona y el momento.
segments: There is a time to sugarcoat bad news and a time to be
direct, so never beat around the bush when someone needs a clear answer.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que suaviza «The bank fired Sara» al hablar con una amiga.

choices.text: Sara was kicked out of the bank last week.
Sara was simply fired from the bank last week.
Sara was let go by the bank last week.

feedback.es: Let go conserva el significado de fire pero sin crudeza; las otras dos opciones son directas o incluso agresivas.

hint.es: Busca la expresión que dice lo mismo que fired, pero con delicadeza.

origin.text: Mia wants to tell a friend that Sara lost her job at the bank last week. She would like to sound kind, not blunt.

prompt.es: Completa: «Mi tío está entre trabajos ahora mismo.»

feedback.es: Between jobs es el eufemismo fijo: siempre con el plural jobs.

hint.es: Es el plural de la palabra que significa «empleo».

origin.text: My uncle lost his job in March. He never says he is unemployed; he says he is between ___ right now.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Mi abuela falleció el año pasado.»

answer.text: My grandmother passed away last year
accepted: My grandmother passed away last year
Last year my grandmother passed away

feedback.es: Passed away es un verbo frasal de una sola unidad: el sujeto va antes y el tiempo al final.

hint.es: El verbo con away va justo después del sujeto.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con lo que quiere decir en realidad.

pairs: We had to let him go.
She is between jobs at the moment.

pairs.es: está sin empleo, dicho con tacto

pairs: Your work is not the best, I'm afraid.

feedback.es: Cada eufemismo cambia la palabra cruda (fire, unemployed, bad, die) por otra que protege los sentimientos.

pairs: We had to let him go.
She is between jobs at the moment.

pairs.es: está sin empleo, dicho con tacto

pairs: Your work is not the best, I'm afraid.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué efecto buscaba la directora con sus palabras.

choices.text: To soften the news without changing what was really happening.
To avoid saying that any colleagues would actually lose their jobs.
To show the team that the difficult year was not the company's fault.

feedback.es: Nadie duda de lo ocurrido: los eufemismos suavizan la forma de la noticia, no su contenido.

origin.audio: Last Friday our manager called the whole team together. She began gently: As you know, the company has had a difficult year, and I'm afraid we have to let three colleagues go. She never said fired, and she never said the word unemployed either. Afterwards Mia told me that her brother is between jobs too, and that he hates that word. I think the manager chose her words carefully, although nobody was in any doubt about what had happened.

prompt.es: Completa: «Decir «desempleado» a un amigo puede sonar demasiado brusco.»

feedback.es: Blunt describe la palabra directa que no protege los sentimientos del oyente.

origin.text: Saying «unemployed» to a friend who has just lost his job may sound too ___. Many people say «between jobs» instead.

prompt.es: ¿Qué opina realmente el jefe de la presentación?

choices.text: He is very pleased with it, and only suggests a shorter ending.
He is disappointed with it, but he says so gently.
He is not interested in it, and has no advice to give Leo.

feedback.es: «Not the best» es una atenuación: dice menos de lo que siente, y la oferta de ayuda confirma que hay algo que mejorar.

origin.text: Thank you for your presentation, Leo. It was not the best I have seen this year, and I wonder whether the ending could be a little shorter next time. Do let me know if you would like some help.

prompt.es: Escucha: ¿qué da a entender «his health had not been the best»?

choices.text: That he had seemed healthy until the very last day.
That he had neglected his health for many years.
That he had been ill for quite a long time.

feedback.es: La atenuación «not the best» para la salud de un anciano indica una mala salud prolongada, dicha con delicadeza.

origin.audio: Hello, Mrs Clarke. I'm calling about your father. I'm afraid he passed away this morning. He was elderly, and his health had not been the best for a while, but the family was with him, and he was not in any pain.

prompt.es: Completa: «Los agentes inmobiliarios llaman «acogedor» a un apartamento muy pequeño.»

feedback.es: Cosy es el eufemismo inmobiliario clásico: suena agradable, pero el mensaje real es «muy pequeño».

origin.text: Estate agents rarely say «tiny». They call a very small flat «___», which is a typical euphemism.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Por desgracia, tuvimos que despedir a tres personas.»

answer.text: Sadly we had to let three people go

feedback.es: Let + persona + go separa la expresión: los tres trabajadores se colocan entre let y go.

prompt.es: ¿Por qué el autor escribe «passed away» y no «died»?

choices.text: To show kindness and respect towards a sad family.
To make the news sound less certain than it really was.
To use the formal wording that every letter needs.

feedback.es: En un mensaje de pésame, passed away muestra respeto y cariño; no oculta la muerte, solo la dice con delicadeza.

origin.text: Dear Mrs Kaur, we were very sad to hear that your father passed away last week. He was a kind elderly man, and he will be missed by everyone on the street. If there is anything we can do, please ask.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué opina realmente el hablante sobre la comida.

choices.text: He found the food good enough, and plans to return soon.
He was disappointed by the food, though he says it mildly.
He was disappointed by the service, though he says it mildly.

feedback.es: La atenuación not the best y la decisión de cocinar en casa revelan que la comida decepcionó.

origin.audio: We went to the new restaurant on Saturday. The service was friendly and the room was lovely, but the food, well, let's say it was not the best I have had this year. I think I will cook at home for a while.

prompt.es: Completa: «Leo preguntó si el señor mayor había fallecido.»

feedback.es: Las preguntas de sí o no transmitidas llevan whether o if, con el sujeto antes del verbo.

origin.text: Leo was worried about the old man next door. He asked Sara ___ the elderly man had passed away, but she said he was only in hospital.
